- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often overshoots early in the horizon; cap peak forecasts or adjust downward after 3–5 days.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent mean) — apply smoothing or lagged decay to prevent overshoot.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative, model often fails to correct — reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, adjust downward by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.27–0.30), model tends to underestimate — add 1–2% bias upward for next 3–5 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early (days 1–7) — apply 1–3% downward correction for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
